close_reason: OSCAL compatible via separate pkix-lint-oscal crate; no core changes needed; poam-item+risk is closest construct; gaps documented in notes
notes:
OSCAL Assessment Results compatibility analysis:

Closest OSCAL construct: poam-item with risk.status=deviation-approved.

Field mapping:
- id -> prop(name=deviation-id) on poam-item (OSCAL requires UUID as primary key; human-readable id preserved as prop)
- target_lint -> prop(name=lint-id, ns=pkix-lint) on risk observation (no native OSCAL lint rule concept)
- scope (IssuerDnContains) -> prop (no native OSCAL subject selector for cert issuer DN)
- effective_start/end -> risk-log.entry.start + risk.deadline
- action=Suppress -> risk.status=accepted or false-positive (good fit)
- action=DowngradeSeverityTo -> prop(name=effective-severity) on risk (no native OSCAL severity adjustment action)
- justification -> risk.description (good fit)
- authorized_by -> risk-log.entry logged-by (OSCAL requires party UUID declared in metadata; current free-text needs a prop)

Gaps: scope mismatch (biggest), authorized_by party reference, target_lint no native equivalent, DowngradeSeverityTo has no OSCAL action type.

Implementation path: separate pkix-lint-oscal crate with fn to_poam_item(d: &Deviation) -> OscalPOAMItem. No changes to Deviation struct required. Two optional additions for cleaner OSCAL: id_uuid: Option<Uuid> and scope_subject_uuid: Option<Uuid> for native OSCAL linking.
